# Affine: current miner protocol and operating guide

Updated October 9, 2026. Network: Bittensor Finney, subnet 120.
Code: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine
Availability: https://affine.io/mining.json
Dashboard: https://affine.io/

## Current availability

The restored completed-answer MATH learner published epoch 86 on October 9,
2026 at 04:10:25 UTC. Public discovery, the signed pointer/manifest and the complete
approved source archive were independently read back successfully. The opening
includes 253 activated identities and the compact eight-rollout contract below.
This establishes public miner access; submission, training and learning results
are reported separately as they occur.

Mining is available only when mining.json reports `accepting_submissions: true`
and its authenticated opening has not expired. Between updates it may report
`between_epochs`; a binding fault reports `discovery_binding_error`. Always read
current discovery rather than treating epoch 86 or this guide as a live window.

Epoch 85's legacy full-vocabulary opening is closed. Its submissions are archived.
The earlier statement that it enforced v5 sampling was incorrect: its signed
manifest lacked that contract. Do not submit further work to epoch 85.
Chain weight submission and payouts are disabled during this qualification.

The authoritative inputs are the signed current pointer, signed epoch manifest,
and exact approved source archive. This guide describes the restored contract;
it cannot extend a deadline or override a signed opening. GitHub main can also
contain research code that the signed source has not activated.

## Task, model and batch rules

- Environment: `affine_math`, `prime-v1-2-completed-math`.
- Taskset: 7,496 usable MATH problems; 6,746 available for mining and 750 held out.
  Use only task indices advertised for mining in the signed opening.
- Base: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct`, original pinned revision
  `ef9926d75ab1d54532f6a30dd5e760355eb9aa4d`.
  After each update, download the checkpoint in the new manifest, not the base
  again and not a previous epoch's learned checkpoint.
- Each batch covers one task under one epoch/checkpoint and contains exactly
  eight distinct rollouts: four completed correct answers and four completed
  incorrect answers (K=4, L=4).
- Maximum: three task batches per registered UID per epoch. Extra rollouts on
  the same task do not earn more points. Duplicate task indices across miners
  in the same epoch receive zero contribution points under the uniqueness rule.
- Output budget: 2048 tokens. The signed harness sets the actual limit.
- Sampling: temperature 0.8, top-p 1, prescribed miner-bound v5 draws.
- Allowed attempt nonces: integers 0 through 999, per miner/task/epoch.
  All eight rollouts require distinct nonces and distinct generated content.

The completed-answer rule requires a nonempty balanced final `\boxed{...}`.
Missing, empty or unfinished final boxes are unresolved. They fill neither the
success nor failure quota and are excluded from training. Hitting the token cap
is not itself a wrong answer; a completed box is graded normally by the native
math grader. Grader/runtime errors are not negative examples.

## Proof and upload contract

The current source archive SHA256 is:
`74f132382afb89236d3fc2300fa6917761e5a4c0e24c8e20ea24a0410ddaebe3`.
Always authenticate the actual opening; a future source upgrade changes this pin.

Sampling version: `forced-inverse-cdf-prefill-miner-bound-v5`.
Random draws bind epoch randomness, checkpoint, authenticated miner identity,
task, nonce, turn and token position. Miners may search the allowed nonces and
select qualifying outcomes. Different nonces do not guarantee different text;
content deduplication still applies. Reusing a proof from another epoch or
checkpoint does not establish validity for the new one.

Upload generated tokens, selected-token log probabilities, TOPLOC fingerprints
and native outcome metadata through the approved client. Do not upload full
vocabulary probability arrays. The verifier independently recomputes the full
distribution and checks the prescribed sampling draws, TOPLOC and environment
outcome. TOPLOC alone does not establish sampling consistency. Calibrated
prefill checks use exact cached replay to adjudicate ambiguous cases.

Batch transport: `small-commitment-pairs-v2`, with
`selected-token-logprobs-v1` and lossless compression. The client uploads bounded
per-batch proofs and small training documents, then their signed commitment.
Capabilities are encrypted to registered miner identities. Miners need no
permanent R2 credentials and cannot read other miners' private current uploads.
`direct-r2-v1` on the outer discovery pointer describes storage access; it does
not mean full-vocabulary batch transport.

Token-only and three-way research verification profiles are not activated.

## Registration and runtime

There is no operator whitelist. A miner needs a current subnet-120 UID, an
Ed25519 hotkey and a valid Affine activation. The next epoch snapshots eligible
identities; registration/activation during an epoch may appear in the next one.

For an already registered Ed25519 hotkey, preview activation:

```sh
python -m subnet.register --wallet YOUR_WALLET --hotkey YOUR_ED25519_HOTKEY
```

Add `--execute` when you intend to submit the activation commitment. This command
does not buy/register a subnet UID. The mining key file contains that activated
32-byte Ed25519 seed as hexadecimal, mode 0600. Never share it or a coldkey.

Qualified inference/audit hardware is H200/SM90. Use CUDA FP32 eager attention,
TF32 disabled and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Qualified core package pins
are torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.14.1 and toploc 0.1.6. Package versions alone do
not establish compatibility with different hardware or numerical settings.
Install the repository and native environment dependencies, then obey the
manifest's exact runtime profile. Training has its own signed runtime.

## Start mining

Clone https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine and update with
`git pull --ff-only` before starting. The public bootstrap now accepts signed
source descriptors using either `read_url` or `url`; both must match if present.
Older bootstrap clients fail on the completed-answer `read_url` descriptor.
The fix retains signature, HTTPS, archive size, SHA256 and membership checks.

Read `authority` and `current_url` from https://affine.io/mining.json only when
it reports an open window. The expected authority public key is:
`3301134b38401196d006a621ac4a772bb4b0e6afa15a7d34a0d1ae5f2c630bcd`.
Set these as `AFFINE_AUTHORITY` and `AFFINE_CURRENT_URL`, then run:

```sh
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 python -B -m subnet.source_bootstrap \
  --authority "$AFFINE_AUTHORITY" \
  --current-url "$AFFINE_CURRENT_URL" \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/affine-approved-source \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.seed \
  --state /absolute/private/affine-miner-state \
  --env-id affine_math --max-batches 3 --search-budget 32
```

32 is a recommended local per-task search budget, not the allowed nonce ceiling.
It gives an eight-rollout quota more room than the old eight-attempt example.
The current approved CLI accepts search budgets from 1 through 128. The protocol
separately permits nonce values 0 through 999; compatible custom miners may use
that full range. Tune the CLI budget within its 128-attempt limit for task
success rates and remaining epoch time. Move on when one outcome is too rare.
A longer search cannot extend the signed upload deadline.

The bootstrap verifies the pointer, manifest and complete source archive, admits
the task snapshot, and executes only that approved source in an isolated fresh
Python process. The client authenticates checkpoint files before inference.
Signed source execution is not a security sandbox.

The command above follows checkpoint changes continuously under the same approved
source. Add `--once` only for a single-epoch smoke test. If the approved source
changes, the client stops and needs a fresh bootstrap.
Alternatively, supervise one-shot runs: poll discovery, start each new epoch once,
inspect its original process after timeouts, and stop using the old checkpoint
when the opening changes. `--once` does not itself watch forever. Do not run
multiple processes sharing the same identity/epoch state or reset the upload
journal to claim duplicate batches. A source upgrade requires a fresh bootstrap.

## Learning, auditing and monitoring

The learner captures committed training documents, checks identity, task,
checkpoint, structure and native completed-answer outcomes, then selects bounded
eligible inputs for training. Expensive proof audits run continuously and do not
gate the training update. Unaudited inputs remain explicitly labelled unaudited.
The trainer preserves its local optimizer state and uploads the successor model
and reports; miners then follow the new checkpoint. Checkpoint publication does
not wait for full vocabulary arrays or a complete network audit.

Independent verifiers sample current and historical immutable commitments and
publish authenticated findings. Reward estimates combine eligible unique task
contributions, accumulated audit evidence and configured penalties. Numerical
ambiguity or infrastructure failure must not be labelled confirmed fraud.
Qualification currently produces evidence/assessments with chain payout disabled.

A completed optimizer update is not proof of learning. Independent held-out
scores track model performance; assess matched checkpoints on the same cohort.
The target is continuous sub-hour epochs. An opening, a submitted batch, an
accepted training input, a completed proof audit and a published update are
separate states and should be reported separately.

## Troubleshooting and references

- Closed discovery: wait for the next authenticated opening; never bypass it.
- Missing capability: confirm registration and Ed25519 activation, then wait
  for a new identity snapshot.
- Source URL failure on `read_url`: update the public bootstrap with `git pull`.
- Source/hash/runtime mismatch: use the advertised archive and exact profile;
  never edit a signed manifest or reuse a different checkpoint.
- No completed batch: inspect native outcomes, unresolved answers, remaining
  time and per-task search budget. Four distinct answers of each class are needed.
- Upload failure after deadline: preserve local evidence and continue next epoch;
  a late submission is not accepted merely because generation began earlier.
